Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 135:

﴿Say: "O my people, act according to your standing.﴾ "According to your standing" means according to the utmost extent of your capacity and ability; it is said makana makanatan (مَكُنَ مَكانَةً) when one establishes himself to the highest degree of establishment. Or it means according to your position and direction in which you are, from their saying makan (مَكانٌ) and makanah (مَكانَةٌ), like maqam (مَقامٌ) and maqamah (مَقامَةٌ). Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, read makanatikum (مَكاناتِكم) in the plural in the entire Qur'an, and it is an imperative of threat. The meaning is: persist in your disbelief and your enmity. ﴿Indeed, I am acting﴾ according to what you have been upon of perseverance and steadfastness in Islam. The threat in the form of a command is an intensification of the warning, as if the one being threatened wants to torment him, resolved upon it, so the command drives him toward what leads to it; and it records that from the one being threatened nothing but evil can come, like one commanded to do something who cannot be dissuaded from it. ﴿So you will soon know who will have the good outcome of the abode.﴾ If man (مَنِ) is made interrogative, meaning "which of us will have the good outcome of the abode, the good abode for which God created this abode," then its position is nominative, and the verb of knowledge (تَعْلَمُونَ) is suspended from it. If it is made a relative/declarative clause, then it is accusative by virtue of taʿlamun (تَعْلَمُونَ), i.e., "you will soon recognize the one to whom the outcome of the abode belongs." In this there is, together with the warning, fairness in speech and good manners, and an indication of the warner's certainty that he is right. Hamzah and al-Kisai read yakunu (يَكُونُ) with the ya', because the feminine marking of ʿaqibah (العاقِبَةِ) is not real. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper.﴾ He placed "the wrongdoers" (الظّالِمُونَ) in place of "the disbelievers" (الكافِرِينَ) because it is more general and more beneficial.

(p-184) ﴿And they assigned﴾, i.e., the idolaters of the Arabs, ﴿to God a share of what He has created (dhara')﴾, i.e., created, ﴿of the tilth and the cattle﴾, ﴿a portion, and they say: "This is for God," by their claim, "and this is for our partners." So what is for their partners does not reach God, and what is for God does reach their partners.﴾ It is related that they would designate a portion of their crops and livestock for God and spend it on guests and the poor, and a portion of them for their gods, spending it on their attendants (sadana) and slaughtering it at their shrines. Then, if they saw that what they had designated for God was more pure (azka), they would exchange it for what belonged to their gods; and if they saw that what belonged to their gods was more pure, they would leave it to them, out of love for their gods.

In His saying ﴿what He has created (dhara')﴾ there is an alert to the extent of their folly, for they associated with the Creator in His creation a lifeless object that has no power over anything, and then they preferred it over Him by making the purer portion its own. In His saying ﴿by their claim﴾ there is an alert that this is something they invented, which God did not command them. Al-Kisa'i read the vowel ﴿ḍamm﴾ (u) in both places, and it is a dialectal form of it; the vowel kasr (i) has also come in it, as in al-widd and al-wuddu (love). ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, i.e., this their judgment.

**Verse 6:137** — *"And thus [too] has their associates made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children"*: that is, like that adornment in the division of offerings (ومِثْلُ ذَلِكَ التَّزْيِينِ في قِسْمَةِ القُرْبانِ). *"[Their] killing"*: by burying them alive (بِالوَأْدِ) and by slaughtering them for their gods (ونَحْرِهِمْ لِآلِهَتِهِمْ). *"Their associates"*: from among the jinn or from among the custodians (al-sadana) of the idols (مِنَ الجِنِّ أوْ مِنَ السَّدَنَةِ), and it is the subject (fa'il) of zayyana. Ibn ʿAmir read zuyyina (passive), with the killing as the deputy subject (naʾib al-fa'il), which is the verb's agent-noun construction (al-bina' lil-maf'ul) on the killing; he put the children in the accusative and the associates in the genitive, by attributing the killing to the associates while separating them with the object (bi-idafat al-qatl ilayhi mafsulan baynahuma bi-maf'ulihi). This is weak in Arabic grammar (al-'arabiyya) and is counted among the poetic necessities (darurat al-shi'r), as in his saying:

*"So I pushed her with a push, as the she-camel's push by Abi Muzadah"* (fazajjtuha bi-mazajatin / zajja al-qalusi abi muzadah).

It was also read with the passive voice, with the genitive on "their children" and the nominative on "their associates" (wa-rufi'a shurakauhum), by supposing a verb omitted that is indicated by zayyana. *"That they may destroy them"*: that they may ruin them (li-yuhlikuhum) by misleading (bi-l-ighwa'). *"And that they may confuse for them their religion"*: that they may mix up for them what they were upon of the religion of Isma'il, or what it was obligatory upon them to adhere to in religion. The lam is for causation (lil-ta'lil) if the adornment is from the devils, and for consequence (al-'aqiba) if it is from the custodians.

*"And had Allah willed, they would not have done it"*: the polytheists would not have done what was made attractive to them, or the associates would not have made the adornment, or both groups together would not have done all of that. *"So leave them and what they fabricate"*: their fabrication, or what they fabricate of falsehood (al-ifk).

﴿And they say, "These﴾ is a demonstrative referring to what they had designated for their gods. ﴿are cattle and tilth, forbidden (ḥijr)﴾. Ḥijr is on the pattern fiʿl in the sense of maf‘ūl (ḥarām, "forbidden"), like dhibḥ (slaughter), and it is used the same way for the singular and the plural, and for the masculine and the feminine. It is also read as ḥujr with a ḍamma, and as ḥaraj, meaning "restricted." ﴿None may eat of them except whom we wish﴾: they mean that only the servants of the idols and the men, to the exclusion of the women, may eat of them. ﴿By their claim﴾: without any proof. ﴿And cattle whose backs are forbidden﴾: they mean the baḥāʾir (she-camels whose ears were slit and who were released), the sawāʾib (animals released for their gods), and the ḥawāmī (stallions set free after a certain number of covers). ﴿And cattle over which they do not mention the name of God﴾: at slaughter, but they mention the names of the idols over them. It is also said that they do not perform the pilgrimage riding on their backs. ﴿Fabricating against Him﴾: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar), because what they said is an invention (taqawwul) against God, glorified and exalted be He. The prepositional phrase (ʿalayhi) is connected either to qālū ("they said") or to a deleted element which serves as its adjective, or it is in the accusative of circumstance (ḥāl), or it is an object of purpose (maf‘ūl lahu), and the prepositional phrase is connected to it or to the deleted element. ﴿He will requite them for what they used to invent﴾: "for" (bi) here means "because of," or it is a substitute for (badal) what they used to invent.

(p-185) ﴿And they say: What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives﴾ — meaning the fetuses of the baḥāʾir and the sawāʾib. ﴿Exclusively for our males﴾: it is lawful for the males only, to the exclusion of the females, if it is born alive, according to His saying: ﴿But if it is dead, they all share in it﴾. Thus males and females are equal in it. The feminine form of khāliṣah is used in accordance with the sense, since what is in the wombs (mā) carries the meaning of fetuses (al-ajinnah). For this reason ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of Abū Bakr, and Ibn ʿĀmir read takun with the tāʾ, while he (ʿĀṣim) and Ibn Kathīr disagreed with them regarding mayyitatan, reading it with a naṣb (fatḥah) like the others. Or the tāʾ in it is for emphasis (mubālaghah), as in the transmission of ash-shiʿr, or it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) like al-ʿāfiyah, placed in the position of khāliṣ. It was also read in the accusative (naṣb), as a verbal noun for emphasis (maṣdar muʾakkid), with the predicate being li-dhukūrinā; or as a ḥāl (circumstantial clause) from the pronoun in the adverbial phrase (ẓarf), not from the one in li-dhukūrinā, nor from al-dhukūr, because it (the ḥāl) does not precede the implied operator (al-ʿāmil al-maʿnawī) nor its own referent (ṣāḥibuhā) which is in the genitive (majrūr). It was also read khāliṣun with the nominative and accusative, and khāliṣatun with the nominative and as an idāfah to the pronoun, on the basis that it is a substitute (badal) for mā, or a second subject (mubtadaʾ thānī). The intended meaning of it is what was alive. The masculine form in fīhi is because the intended sense of mayyitah encompasses both male and female, so the masculine was given precedence.

﴿He will recompense them for their description﴾ — i.e., the recompense for their describing a lie against Allah, glorified and exalted is He, regarding forbidding and permitting, from His saying: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie﴾. ﴿Indeed He is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 140:

﴿They have certainly lost who have killed their children﴾ He means by them the Arabs who used to kill their daughters for fear of captivity and poverty. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read *qattalu* with the doubling (shaddah), in the sense of intensification (al-taksir, i.e. repetition or multiplicity of the act). ﴿in foolishness, without knowledge﴾ due to the lightness of their intellect and their ignorance that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is the provider of their children, not they themselves. Its being in the accusative (nasb) may be as a circumstantial state (hal) or as a verbal noun (masdar). ﴿and have forbidden what Allah has provided for them﴾ of the baha'ir (she-camels whose ears were slit and were forbidden) and the like. ﴿as a fabrication against Allah﴾ it admits the aspects mentioned in similar cases. ﴿They have certainly gone astray and were not guided﴾ to the truth and what is correct.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 141:

﴿And it is He who produced gardens﴾ of vines, ﴿trellised and untrellised﴾: trellised, meaning raised up on what supports them; untrellised, meaning lying spread upon the surface of the earth. It is said that the trellised ones are those that people planted and then trellised, and the untrellised ones are those that grew in the wilderness and the mountains. ﴿And the date palm and the crops, varying in their produce﴾: its fruit that is eaten, in its form and its quality. The pronoun refers to the crops, and the rest is analogous to it; or it refers to the date palm, and the crops are included in its ruling by virtue of being conjoined to it; or it refers to all of them, on the assumption "all of that" or "each one of these two," and "varying" is a future-referring circumstantial clause (ḥāl muqaddarah), because that was not the case at the time of production. ﴿And the olives and the pomegranates, similar and dissimilar﴾: some of their individual kinds resemble one another in color and taste, and some do not resemble one another. ﴿Eat of its fruit﴾: of the fruit of each one of these. ﴿When it bears fruit﴾, even if it has not ripened and has not yet become fully ready. It is said that its purpose is the permission of the owner to eat from it before the payment of God Most High's right. ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: it intends by this what used to be given in charity on the day of harvest, not the prescribed zakat, because zakat was made obligatory in Medina and this verse is Meccan.

It is said that the zakat is meant, and the verse is Medinan, and the command to give it on the day of harvest is so that attention is paid to it at that time, so that it is not delayed beyond the time of payment, and so that it is known that the obligation arises at the time of ripening, not at the time of cleaning. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ḥiṣādihi with a kasra on the ḥā', and this is a dialectal variant of it.

﴿And do not be wasteful﴾ in giving charity, like His saying, Exalted is He: "and do not extend it fully outstretched" (Q. 17:29). ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wasteful﴾: He does not approve of their action.(p-186)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 142–143:

﴿And of the cattle, some for burden and some for slaughter (ḥamūlatan wa farshan)﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf) upon "gardens" (jannāt), meaning: and He produced from the cattle that which bears loads and that which is for slaughter (lil-dhabḥ), or that which provides the spread (farsh), i.e., the woven material made from their hair, wool and fleece. It has been said: the large ones suitable for carrying, and the small ones close to the ground, like the spread laid upon them. ﴿Eat of what God has provided for you﴾ — eat of what He has made lawful for you from it. ﴿And do not follow the steps of Satan﴾ — in declaring things lawful and unlawful on the basis of your own selves. ﴿Indeed, he is to you a manifest enemy﴾ — whose enmity is evident.

﴿Eight pairs (thamāniyata azwāj)﴾ is a substitute (badal) for "burden and spread", or the object of "eat". "And do not follow" is an interjection (muʿtariḍ) between them, or a verb implied by it. Or it is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from "what", in the sense of "of varied kinds" or "of many kinds". The "zawj" (pair) is that which has with it another of its kind to pair with it; it may also be said of the two together, but the intended meaning here is the first. ﴿Of the sheep, two (min al-ḍaʾn ithnayn)﴾ — two pairs: the ram and the ewe. It is a substitute for "eight". It has been read as "ithnān" (two) in the nominative as a beginning (ibtidāʾ). "Ḍaʾn" (sheep) is a collective noun (ism jins), like "ibil" (camels); its plural is "ḍaʾin", or it is the plural of "ḍāʾin", like "tājir" and "tajr". It has also been read with a fatḥah on the hamza, and this is a dialectal form of it.

﴿And of the goats, two (wa min al-maʿz ithnayn)﴾ — the he-goat and the she-goat. Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir and Yaʿqub read it with a fatḥah (al-maʿaz), and it is the plural of "māʿiz", like "ṣāḥib" and "ṣaḥb", "ḥāris" and "ḥaras". It has also been read "al-miʿzā". ﴿Say: Are the two males (al-dhakarayn) forbidden, or the two females (al-unthayayn)?⌉ — the male of the sheep and the male of the goat. ﴿Or what the wombs of the two females contain?⌉ — "am" here means "or" concerning their females; the "two males" and "two females" are governed by "ḥarrama" (forbade). ﴿Or what the wombs of the two females have conceived?⌉ — or what the females of both kinds have carried, whether male or female. ﴿Inform me with knowledge⌉ — with a matter known, indicating that God Most High has forbidden any of that. ﴿If you are truthful⌉ — in your claim that He has forbidden it.

and of the camels two and of the cattle two. Say: "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain?" as already mentioned. The meaning is a denial that Allah has forbidden any of the four kinds, whether male or female, or what their females carry, in refutation of them. For they used to forbid the males of the livestock at one time, and the females at another time, and their young, however they were, at another time, claiming that Allah had forbidden them.

﴿Or were you witnesses﴾, rather, were you present and witnessing? ﴿When Allah enjoined this upon you﴾, when He enjoined on you this prohibition, since you do not believe in any prophet, so there is no way for you to know such matters except by witnessing or hearing.

﴿Who then is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah﴾, so that he attributes to Him the prohibition of what He did not prohibit. The intended ones are their leaders who established this practice, or ʿAmr ibn Luhayy ibn Qamaʿa (ʿAmr ibn Luhayy ibn Qamaʿah), who founded it. ﴿To mislead people without knowledge. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

Say: "I find not in what has been revealed to me" (﴿قُلْ لا أجِدُ في ما أُوحِيَ إلَيَّ﴾), meaning in the Qur'an, or in what has been revealed to me in general. This indicates that prohibition is known through revelation (wahy), not through whim (hawa).

"Forbidden" (﴿مُحَرَّمًا﴾) means a forbidden food, "for an eater who eats it" (﴿عَلى طاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ﴾), "unless it be carrion" (﴿إلا أنْ يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً﴾), meaning unless the food be carrion. Ibn Kathir and Hamzah read "takuna" with a ta' (تَكُونُ), because the predicate is feminine. Ibn Amir reads it with a ya' (يَكُونَ). He reads "maytatan" in the nominative, taking "kana" (كانَ) here as the complete verb (al-tammah), meaning "unless there occurs carrion."

﴿أوْ دَمًا مَسْفُوحًا﴾, "or poured-forth blood," is conjoined (ʿataf) to "an anna" together with what follows it, meaning: unless there is the existence of carrion or poured-forth blood. "Masfuh" means poured out, like blood in the veins, not like the liver and spleen.

﴿أوْ لَحْمَ خِنْزِيرٍ فَإنَّهُ رِجْسٌ﴾, "or the flesh of swine, for it is an abomination," means that the pig, or its flesh, is filthy because it habitually eats impurities, or it is foul and makes its eater foul.

﴿أوْ فِسْقًا﴾, "or an abomination of transgression," is conjoined to "lahma khinzir" (the flesh of swine). What lies between them is a parenthetical (i'tiraḍ) explanation of the reason (ta'lil).

﴿أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ بِهِ﴾, "that over which other than God has been invoked," is a qualifying clause describing it. That which is slaughtered in the name of an idol is called "fisq" because of its extreme transgression. It is also permissible for "fisqan" to be an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu) of "uhilla," and it is conjoined to "yakuna," and the implied pronoun in it refers back to what the implied pronoun in "yakunu" refers back to.

﴿فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ﴾, "But whoever is compelled," means whoever is driven by necessity (darura) to consume any of those things, ﴿غَيْرَ باغٍ﴾ "neither desiring (it) [in transgression] over one like him in need," ﴿وَلا عادٍ﴾ "nor exceeding" the measure of necessity. ﴿فَإنَّ رَبَّكَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, "then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful," meaning He does not hold him to account.

The verse is muhkam (definitive, not abrogated), because it indicates that he did not find, in what was revealed to him for that purpose, any prohibition other than these. That does not preclude the prohibition of something else from being revealed. Therefore it is not valid to use this verse as evidence for the abrogation (naskh) of the Book by a solitary report (khabar al-wahid), nor for the permissibility of other things, except together with the presumption of continuity (istishab), meaning the presumption that the original state persists.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 6, verses 146–147:

﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾: every animal that has a toe (*isba'*), such as the camel, beasts of prey, and birds. It is also said: every animal with a talon (*mikhlab*) and every animal with a hoof (*hafir*). The hoof is called a claw (*zufr*) metaphorically (*majaz*). Perhaps the cause of the universal prohibition is their wrongdoing (*zulm*). ﴿And from the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fats﴾: the *thurub* (the fat covering the intestines) and the fat of the kidneys. The genitive construction (*idafah*) is for emphasis of connection. ﴿Except what their backs carry﴾: except what clings to their backs. ﴿Or the entrails﴾: or what envelops the intestines. It is the plural of *hawiyah*, or of *hawiya'* like *qasi'a'* and *qawasi'*, or of *hawiyyah* like *safinah* and *safa'in*. It is also said that it is conjoined (*'atf*) to "their fats," and that "or" (*aw*) carries the meaning of "and." ﴿Or what is mixed with a bone﴾: this is the fat of the buttock, since it is joined to the coccyx (*'usʿus*). ﴿That﴾: the prohibition, or the recompense. ﴿We recompensed them for their rebellion (*baghy*)﴾: because of their wrongdoing. ﴿And indeed We are truthful﴾: in the report, or in the promise and the threat.

﴿So if they deny you, say: your Lord is the Possessor of vast mercy﴾: He gives you respite despite your denial, so do not be deceived by His respite, for He does not neglect. ﴿And His punishment will not be averted from the guilty people﴾ when it descends. Or: He is the Possessor of vast mercy toward the obedient and the Possessor of severe punishment toward the guilty. Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 6, verse 148:

﴿Those who associated partners with God will say﴾: a report about the future, and the occurrence of what it reports is a proof of its miraculousness. ﴿If God had willed, we would not have associated partners, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything﴾, meaning: if He had willed the opposite of that with a will that He approves, as in His saying, ﴿Then if He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [6:149]. ﴿We did not do so, nor did our fathers﴾. By this they meant that they were upon the truth that is legislated and approved by God, not that they were making an excuse for committing these abominations by God's willing them from them, such that their blame would stand as evidence for the al-Mu'tazilah (the Mu'tazilites). This is supported by His saying: ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾, meaning: a denial like this denial of yours, in that God, exalted is He, prohibited shirk and did not forbid what they forbade. Those before them denied the messengers. He conjoined *āba'unā* (our fathers) to the pronoun in *ashrakna* (we associated) without emphasis on the separation with *lā* (لا). ﴿Until they tasted Our might﴾, which We sent down upon them because of their denial. ﴿Say: Do you have any knowledge﴾, meaning any matter that is known and that can validly be used as an argument, ﴿on the basis of which you claim?﴾ ﴿So that you bring it out for us﴾ (p-188), meaning that you show it to us. ﴿You follow nothing but conjecture﴾, meaning in this matter you follow nothing but conjecture. ﴿And you are only guessing﴾, meaning you are lying against God, glorified and exalted is He. In this is evidence for the prohibition of following conjecture, especially in the fundamentals of belief (*uṣūl*, the foundational articles of faith). Perhaps that applies where a definitive proof contradicts it, since the verse is about that case.

﴿Say: "Then to God belongs the conclusive proof."﴾ This is the clear evidence that has reached the utmost firmness and strength in establishing (a claim). Alternatively, it means that its holder has thereby reached the soundness of his claim. It derives from *ḥajj* in the sense of intending (*qaṣd*), as if it intends to establish the ruling and seeks it.

﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all.﴾ By granting you success in it (*tawfiq*) and compelling you toward it. But He willed the guidance of some people and the misguidance of others.

﴿Say: "Bring forth your witnesses" (هَلُمَّ شُهَداءَكُمُ).﴾ That is, bring them here. Here هَلُمَّ is an *ism fi'l* (a demonstrative verb-noun, a noun functioning as a verb) that does not inflect according to the people of the Ḥijāz. According to the Banū Tamīm, it is a verb that takes feminine and plural forms. According to the Basrans, its original form is هَا لِمَ مَن لَمْ, and when it is used as a command, the alif is dropped to indicate the sukūn on the lām, since this is the original form. According to the Kufans, its original form is هَلْ أمْ, so the hamza was dropped by transferring its vowel onto the lām. This view is far-fetched, because هَلْ does not enter the imperative. The word is transitive, as in this verse, and intransitive, as in His saying: هَلُمَّ إلَيْنا (come to us).

﴿who testify that God has forbidden this.﴾ That is, their leaders in it. He summoned them so that the proof would be binding upon them, and so that their inability to respond would reveal their misguidance, and that they have no ground to stand on, like one who merely follows them in taqlid. For this reason he restricted "the witnesses" by the genitive construction and described them by what requires that they be known.

﴿If they testify, do not testify with them.﴾ That is, do not confirm them in it. Clarify its corruption to them, for accepting it is agreement with them in false testimony.

﴿And do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs.﴾ The use of the apparent noun in place of the pronoun indicates that the one who denies the signs is only a follower of his desire, and that the follower of proof can only be one who affirms it.

﴿And those who do not believe in the Hereafter.﴾ Like the worshippers of idols.

﴿and they ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾ That is, they make for Him equals (*ʿadīl*).

﴿Say: "Come!"﴾ *Ta'alaw* is an imperative from *ta'alli* (rising up, elevation). Its original use is for someone on high to call someone below, and its use was then extended generally.

﴿*Atlu*﴾ means "I recite" (*aqra'*). ﴿*Ma harrama rabbukum*﴾ is in the accusative as the object of *atlu*. *Ma* may be a relative pronoun or a verbal-noun (*masdariyya*) particle. It could also be an interrogative in the accusative governed by *harrama*, with the whole clause then serving as the object of *atlu*, since *atlu* here has the sense of *aqul* ("I say"). The sense would then be: "Say, what your Lord has forbidden." ﴿*'Alaykum*﴾ is attached either to *harrama* or to *atlu*.

﴿*Allā tushrikū bihi*﴾ means "that you do not associate anything with Him," that is, *lā tushrikū bihi*, so that the command can be coordinated with it (*'atf al-amr 'alayhi*). ﴿*Shay'an*﴾ may be a verbal noun (*masdar*) or an object (*maf'ul*).

Like His saying: "fear of poverty" (Q. 17:31).

﴿*Nahnu narzuqukum wa iyyahum*﴾ is a refutation of the reason that they used to act upon, and an argument against it.

﴿*Dhalikum*﴾ is a reference to what has been mentioned in detail. ﴿*Wassakum bihi*﴾ means "to preserve it." ﴿*La'allakum ta'qilun*﴾ means "that you may be guided aright," for the perfection of reason (*'aql*) is guidance (*rushd*).

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 152:

﴿And do not approach the wealth of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾, i.e., by the course of action that is best for his wealth, such as preserving it and making it grow.

﴿until he reaches his maturity (ashuddahu)﴾, i.e., until he becomes an adult (baligh). Ashudd is the plural of shiddah, like ni'mah and an'um, or of shadd, like surr and asurr. It is also said to be a singular noun, like anta'.

﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾, i.e., with fairness and equity. ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, i.e., only what it can bear and what does not cause it hardship. He mentioned this right after the command, meaning: fully giving what is due is difficult for you, so you are to do what is within your capacity, and whatever lies beyond that is pardoned for you.

﴿And when you speak﴾, in a judgment or the like. ﴿then be just﴾ in it. ﴿even if it concerns a near relative﴾, even if the one spoken to or about is among your kin. ﴿And fulfill the covenant of God﴾, i.e., what has been enjoined upon you of adhering to justice and discharging the rulings of the Shari'ah. ﴿This He has enjoined upon you that you may remember﴾, that you may take admonition from it. Hamzah, Hafs and al-Kisa'i read tadhakkarun with the dhal lightened wherever it occurs with the letter ta' (in the form tatadhakkarun in the sense of being the ta' of the verb), while the rest read it with the dhal doubled.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 153:

﴿And that this is My path, straight﴾ The reference in it is to what was mentioned in the surah, for it in its entirety is about establishing tawhid (the oneness of God) and prophethood and explaining the sharia (sacred law). Hamza and al-Kisa'i read inna (إنَّ) with a kasra, as a new sentence (isti'naf). Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read it with a fatha and a light (takhfif) pronunciation.

The rest read it with a fatha and a shadda (doubled consonant), with the lam being understood as implied (taqdir al-lam), so that it is a reason (ʿilla) for His saying: "so follow it." Ibn 'Amir read ﴿ṣirāṭī﴾ with a fatha on the ya' (ṣirāṭiya). It has also been read as ﴿wa-hādhā ṣirāṭī﴾, ﴿wa-hādhā ṣirāṭu rabbikum﴾, and ﴿wa-hādhā ṣirāṭu rabbika﴾.

﴿And do not follow the ways (al-subul)﴾ meaning the differing religions, or the paths that follow desire, for the requirement of proof is one, while the requirement of desire is multiple, owing to the difference of natures and customs. ﴿So that it separates you﴾ meaning, so that it divides you and scatters you ﴿from His way﴾, which is the following of revelation and the pursuit of proof. ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾ meaning, the following. ﴿So that you may be God-fearing﴾, meaning, that you may guard against misguidance and division from the truth.

**Then We gave Moses the Book** ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنا مُوسى الكِتابَ﴾ is coordinated (ʿaṭf, grammatical conjunction) with ﴿وصّاكُمْ﴾ ("He has enjoined you"). The particle **ثُمَّ** ("then") indicates either a delay in the report, or a difference in rank. The meaning is as if it were said: "This is what He enjoined upon you, anciently and recently. Then, greater than that, is that We gave Moses the Book." ﴿تَمامًا﴾ ("in completeness") is for honour and blessing.

**"Upon him who did good"** ﴿عَلى الَّذِي أحْسَنَ﴾ means upon everyone who performed it well. This is supported by the recitation (qiraʾah, variant reading) «عَلى الَّذِينَ أحْسَنُوا» ("upon those who did good"), or «عَلى الَّذِي أحْسَنَ تَبْلِيغَهُ» ("upon him who conveyed it well"), referring to Moses, upon whom be the best of prayers and peace. Or it may be read «تَمامًا عَلى ما أحْسَنَهُ», meaning "He perfected it, what He made excellent," i.e., He perfected it in knowledge and legislation, in addition to his knowledge, as a completion for him. It is also read in the nominative (بِالرَّفْعِ), as the predicate (khabar) of an omitted subject (mubtada, grammatical subject), meaning "upon him who is best," or "in the manner which is the best in which Books can be." 

**"And a detailed explanation of all things"** ﴿وَتَفْصِيلا لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾ means a detailed clarification of everything needed in religion. It is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with **تَمامًا** ("completeness"). The accusative (نَصْب, naṣb) of both words may be understood as a purpose (ʿillah), a circumstantial state (ḥāl), or a verbal noun (maṣdar).

**"And guidance and mercy, that perhaps"** ﴿وَهُدًى ورَحْمَةً لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ — **لَعَلَّ** here means the Children of Israel. ﴿بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("they may believe in the meeting with their Lord") means in meeting Him for the recompense.

(p-190) ﴿And this is a Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿We have sent it down; it is blessed﴾, abundant in benefit. ﴿So follow it and be mindful of God, that you may be shown mercy﴾, through following it, which is acting upon what is in it.

﴿Lest you should say﴾: lest you should say, this being the reason (ʿilla) for ﴿We have sent it down﴾. ﴿The Book was sent down only to two groups before us﴾, the Jews and the Christians. The restrictive sense in ﴿innamā﴾ (only) is probably because the well-known surviving heavenly scriptures at that time were none other than their books.

﴿And indeed we were﴾: ﴿in﴾ here is the light (mukhaffafa) form of the heavy (thaqīla) ﴿inna﴾, which is why the differentiating lām (lām al-fāriqa) entered the predicate of ﴿kāna﴾, meaning, "and indeed, we were". ﴿Unaware of their study﴾, meaning their recitation, ﴿heedless﴾: we did not know what it was, or we did not recognize anything like it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 157:

﴿Or [lest] you should say﴾ is conjoined (ʿatf) to the first [clause]. ﴿"Had the Book been sent down to us, we would surely have been better guided than they"﴾ owing to the keenness of our minds and the acuteness of our understanding; and for this reason we have acquired branches of knowledge such as stories, poetry and sermons, [even] though we are unlettered (ummiyyun). ﴿Now there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord﴾: a manifest argument that you recognise. ﴿And a guidance and a mercy﴾ for whoever reflects upon it and acts by it. ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of God﴾ after he has known their truth or has been able to know them. ﴿And turns away from them﴾: he withdraws or turns aside. ﴿from them﴾: he goes astray or leads astray. ﴿We shall requite those who turn away from Our signs with a dreadful punishment﴾: its severity. ﴿for what they used to turn away﴾: by their aversion or their turning others away.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (*Anwar al-Tanzil*) on surah 6, verse 158:

﴿Do they await﴾, that is, what are they waiting for? This refers to the people of Makkah. They were not actually waiting for that, but since it would befall them as it befalls one who awaits, they were likened to those who await. ﴿Unless the angels come to them﴾: the angels of death or of punishment. Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read *ya'tiyahum* with the letter *yā'* (third person) here and in *al-Naḥl*. ﴿Or your Lord comes﴾: that is, His command to punish, or every sign, meaning the signs of the Resurrection and total destruction, based on His saying: ﴿Or some of the signs of your Lord come﴾, meaning the minor signs of the Hour (*ashrāṭ al-sā'ah*, the preliminary portents of the Last Hour).

Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān and al-Barā' ibn 'Āzib (may Allah be pleased with them) narrated: "We were discussing the Hour when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came upon us and said: 'What are you discussing?' We said: 'We are discussing the Hour.' He said: 'It will not be established until you see ten signs before it: the smoke, the beast of the earth, a sinking in the East, a sinking in the West, a sinking in the Arabian Peninsula, the Dajjal (the Antichrist), the rising of the sun from its west, Ya'jūj and Ma'jūj (Gog and Magog), the descent of 'Īsā (peace be upon him), and a fire that will come out from 'Adan.'"

﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith﴾, like the one at the point of death, when the matter has become a direct observation and faith has become a matter of inference.

*Tanfa'u* (﴿تَنْفَعُ﴾) is also read with the letter *tā'* (feminine), because faith (*īmān*) is attributed to a feminine pronoun. ﴿Which did not believe before, or did not earn good through its faith﴾: the phrase ﴿which did not believe before﴾ is a qualifier of *nafsan* (soul). ﴿Or earned good through its faith﴾ is coordinated with *āmanat* (believed), and the meaning is: faith will not benefit a soul at that time if it was not already forward in its faith, or if it was already forward in its faith but did not earn good through it. This is evidence for those who do not consider faith without deeds to be valid. Those who do consider it valid restrict this ruling to that day. The alternation (*tardīd*) is read as making benefit conditional on one of the two matters, in the sense that faith will not benefit a soul that was empty of it; and the coordination with *lam takun* means that faith newly produced at that time will not benefit a soul, even if it earned good through it.

﴿Say: Wait, we too are waiting﴾: this is a warning to them. That is, wait for the coming of one of the three (signs); we too are waiting for it, and at that time success is ours and woe is yours. (p-191)

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 159–160:

﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion﴾ (broke it up, dispersing it), so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it; or, they became divided (firqah) over it. The prayers and peace of Allah be upon him said: "The Jews divided into seventy-one sects, all of which are in the Abyss except one; the Christians divided into seventy-two sects, all of which are in the Abyss except one; and my community will divide into seventy-three sects, all of which are in the Abyss except one." Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fāraqū" (they separated), meaning they cut themselves off (from it). ﴿And they became sects (shiya')﴾: groups, each sect following (tushayyi'u) a leader (imam). ﴿You have nothing to do with them in anything﴾: that is, with regard to questioning about them and their division, or their punishment; or, you are free of them. It was said that this is a prohibition against confronting them, and it is abrogated by the verse of the sword. ﴿Their affair rests only with Allah﴾: He will take charge of their recompense. ﴿Then He will inform them of what they used to do﴾: with punishment.

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times the like thereof﴾: that is, ten good deeds like it, as a bounty from Allah. Ya'qub read "ʿashara" with tanwin and "amthāluhā" in the nominative as a descriptive (ṣifah). This is the least of the multiplications He promised, and the promise has come of seventy and seven hundredfold, and without reckoning. For this reason it was said: the intended meaning of "ten" is abundance, not the exact number. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except the like thereof﴾: as a requirement of justice.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: by diminution of reward or increase of punishment.

The prayers and peace of Allah be upon him said: "The Jews divided into seventy-one sects, all of which are in the Abyss except one; the Christians divided into seventy-two sects, all of which are in the Abyss except one; and my community will divide into seventy-three sects, all of which are in the Abyss except one." Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fāraqū" (they separated), meaning they cut themselves off (from it). ﴿And they became sects (shiya')﴾: groups, each sect following (tushayyi'u) a leader (imam). ﴿You have nothing to do with them in anything﴾: that is, with regard to questioning about them and their division, or their punishment; or, you are free of them. It was said that this is a prohibition against confronting them, and it is abrogated by the verse of the sword. ﴿Their affair rests only with Allah﴾: He will take charge of their recompense. ﴿Then He will inform them of what they used to do﴾: with punishment.

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him is ten times the like thereof﴾: that is, ten good deeds like it, as a bounty from Allah. Ya'qub read "ʿashara" with tanwin and "amthāluhā" in the nominative as a descriptive (ṣifah). This is the least of the multiplications He promised, and the promise has come of seventy and seven hundredfold, and without reckoning. For this reason it was said: the intended meaning of "ten" is abundance, not the exact number. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except the like thereof﴾: as a requirement of justice.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: by diminution of reward or increase of punishment.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 161:

﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path﴾ by revelation and guidance to what He has set up of proofs. ﴿A religion﴾ is in apposition (badal) to the place of "ila sirat" (to a path), since the meaning is: "He has guided me to a path," like His saying: ﴿and guide you to a straight path﴾. Or it is the object (maf'ul) of a suppressed verb indicated by the verb that is pronounced. ﴿Qiyaman﴾ is on the pattern fi'al from qama, like sayyid from sada; it is more emphatic than "mustaqim" in terms of the morphological form (zinah), while "mustaqim" is considered in terms of the grammatical form (sighah). Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿qiyaman﴾ as a verbal noun (masdar) described by it; its regular form would have been "qiwaman" like "iwad" (a verbal noun of 'awada)... ﴿Millata Ibrahim﴾ is an explanatory apposition ('atf bayan) to "dinan." ﴿Hanifan﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from Ibrahim. ﴿And he was not of the polytheists﴾ is conjoined to it.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 162–163:

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying, are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ "My prayer and my rites" means all my worship, or my sacrifice, or my pilgrimage (ḥajj). "My living and my dying" means what I am upon in my life and what I die upon of faith and obedience; or the acts of obedience of life and the good deeds that are attached to death, such as bequest (waṣiyya) and arrangement (tadbīr); or life and death themselves. Nāfi' read maḥyāy with the yā' silent (sukūn), treating the connected reading as if it were a pause (waqf).

﴿No partner has He.﴾ Sincerely for Him, not associating anything else with Him in it.

﴿And with that I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.﴾ "With that" refers to the statement or to the sincerity. "I am the first of the Muslims" because the submission (islām) of every prophet precedes the submission of his community.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 164:

﴿Say, "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?"﴾ — so that I would associate Him in my worship. This is a response to their calling him to worship their gods. ﴿He is the Lord of all things﴾ — a circumstantial clause (hal) in the position of a causal reason for the denial, and as evidence for it, meaning: everything other than Him is a created thing subject to lordship like me, and is not fit for lordship. ﴿And no soul earns [sin] except against itself﴾ — so what you are upon of that (i.e., of this) will not benefit me in seeking a lord other than Him. And ﴿no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾ — a response to their saying: ﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins﴾. ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and He will inform you of that over which you used to differ﴾ — by making clear the right guidance from error and distinguishing the one who is in the truth from the one who is in falsehood.

Commentary of al-Baydawi (Anwar al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 165:

﴿And it is He who has made you successors (khala'if) of the earth﴾ — one of you succeeds another; or successors of God on His earth, in that you exercise authority over it, on the basis that the address is general; or successors of the earlier nations, on the basis that the address is to the believers. ﴿And He has raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ — in nobility and wealth. ﴿That He may try you in what He has given you﴾ — of standing and property. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty﴾ — because what is to come is near, or because He hastens when He wills it. ﴿And indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — He described the punishment without attributing it to Himself, and He described His essence with forgiveness and joined to it the description of mercy, and He used the intensive form (ibn al-mubalagha) and the emphatic lam, to draw attention to the fact that He, exalted is He, is Forgiving in His essence and punishes only by accident, abundant in mercy, exceeding in it, abundant in punishment, lenient in it.

From the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "The surah al-An'am was sent down to me all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels who have a loud sound of glorifying (tasbih) and praising (tahmid). Whoever recites al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels send blessings upon him and seek forgiveness for him, for every verse of the surah al-An'am, for a day and a night."
